title: Rationale for Singapore Being Potential Claimant from Loss and Damage Fund Set Up in COP27
what_it_is: Rationale for Singapore Being Potential Claimant from Loss and Damage Fund Set Up in COP27

sections.label: Singapore as biodiversity donor
sections.summary: Government considers being a donor rather than claimant to maintain global biodiversity, with position open as part of international negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my supplementary question would be would the Government consider being a donor rather than a claimant, given that it behoves us as a developed country to do our part to maintain global biodiversity vis-à-vis countries such as, for example, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which has much larger land and biodiversity resources and also less funding to manage that issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, our position is open, and this is part of negotiations at the international level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will take into consideration all views, Singaporeans as well as the needs of the international community, as we enter the discussion at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

sections.label: Paris Agreement developing country status
sections.summary: Paris Agreement defines developing and developed countries, and Singapore does not belong to the developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In the first reply, if the Member had gone through it in detail, he would notice that I have taken pains to explain that we are discussing this and there is a principle that all parties are adhering to, which is, the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And in the Paris Agreement, there is a clear definition of who the developing countries are and who the developed countries are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And we do not belong to the developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, if the Member is now suggesting that Singapore is a developed country and should be benchmarked to the other developed countries, that is a deviation from the Paris Agreement.
